theses.subject: Banks
theses.thesis: Banks are eligible and rank 2 with a durable trend tag and the highest breadth (0.778) in a market where almost nothing else is eligible. That durability/breadth combination is the strongest coincident support for leadership continuity even though the rank score itself is not predictive. The single validated discipline does not help here (gate_helps false), so this is a modest structural read, not an edge claim. Crowding (1.77) is a size-down caution only — explicitly not a fade.
theses.dissent: The tracker's own backtest says the trend gate did not reduce drawdown on this mean-reverting tape, and Banks' crowding is near the top of the ranks — leadership could be absorption-topping, and a mean-revert snap in the benchmark would hit the most-crowded eligible winner hardest.

falsifier.text: 512800.SS trails the CSI 300 by more than 3% over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Coal
theses.thesis: Coal is rank 1 and the rotation leader, but the detector's own legs undermine it: r10 is slightly negative, Hurst is mean-revert, breadth is only 0.30 (the weakest among the top eligible themes), and durability is a middling 0.48. In a mean-reverting market where the trend gate does not help, a thin, mean-revert, one-narrative leader is the last place to pay up. Avoid is the honest lean when leadership is fragile and the validated discipline is inert.
theses.dissent: Coal is still the nominal leader and one-narrative regimes can persist longer than the trend-health legs suggest; if energy scarcity headlines re-intensify, a mean-revert tag can flip back to trend and the thin breadth can broaden sharply.

falsifier.text: 515220.SS closes above its 20-day high and its breadth reading (0.30) rises above 0.5 before the check-by date
